messages.content: "請您進行一個統計t檢定，以檢查兩個獨立數據集的平均值是否有統計上的差異？第一個數據集，數據集A，包含以下整數：12、15、18、20、22、25、28、30、32、35。第二個數據集，數據集B，包含以下整數：14、17、19、21、23、26、29、31、33、36。請分別以顯著性水平0.05和0.01進行兩次檢定。"

function.name: t_test
function.description: Perform a statistical t-test to check if the means of two independent datasets are statistically different. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

alpha.description: Significance level for the test. Default is 0.05. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
We need to perform t-tests. We have two datasets each of size 10. We need to compute t-statistic and p-value. Use function t_test. We'll call twice: alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.01. Provide results. Let's compute manually or approximate? Let's compute means, variances.

Dataset A: values: 12,15,18,20,22,25,28,30,32,35. Sum = let's compute: 12+15=27, +18=45, +20=65, +22=87, +25=112, +28=140, +30=170, +32=202, +35=237. Mean = 237/10 = 23.7.

Compute variance: sum of squares: 12^2=144, 15^2=225, 18^2=324, 20^2=400, 22^2=484, 25^2=625, 28^2=784, 30^2=900, 32^2=1024, 35^2=1225. Sum = 144+225=369, +324=693, +400=1093, +484=1577, +625=2202, +784=2986, +900=3886, +1024=4910, +1225=6135. Sample variance s^2 = (sum(x^2)-n*mean^2)/(n-1). mean^2 = 23.7^2 = 561.69. n*mean^2 = 10*561.69 = 5616.9. sum(x^2) - n*mean^2 = 6135 - 5616.9 = 518.1. Divide by 9: 518.1/9 = 57.5667. So s_A^2 ≈ 57.57. Standard deviation s_A ≈ sqrt(57.57)=7.59.

Dataset B: values: 14,17,19,21,23,26,29,31,33,36. Sum: 14+17=31, +19=50, +21=71, +23=94, +26=120, +29=149, +31=180, +33=213, +36=249. Mean = 249/10 = 24.9.

Sum of squares: 14^2=196, 17^2=289, 19^2=361, 21^2=441, 23^2=529, 26^2=676, 29^2=841, 31^2=961, 33^2=1089, 36^2=1296. Sum: 196+289=485, +361=846, +441=1287, +529=1816, +676=2492, +841=3333, +961=4294, +1089=5383, +1296=6679. So sum(x^2)=6679. mean^2 = 24.9^2 = 620.01. n*mean^2 = 6200.1. sum(x^2)-n*mean^2 = 6679 - 6200.1 = 478.9. Divide by 9: 478.9/9 = 53.21. So s_B^2 ≈ 53.21. s_B ≈ sqrt(53.21)=7.29.

Now t-test for independent samples with equal variances? Usually we can use Welch's t-test. But function likely uses standard t-test assuming equal variances? Not specified. We'll assume equal variances? Let's compute pooled variance: sp^2 = ((n1-1)s1^2 + (n2-1)s2^2)/(n1+n2-2) = (9*57.57 + 9*53.21)/18 = (518.13 + 478.89)/18 = 997.02/18 = 55.335. sp = sqrt(55.335)=7.44.

Standard error of difference: SE = sp * sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2) = 7.44 * sqrt(0.1 + 0.1) = 7.44 * sqrt(0.2) = 7.44 * 0.4472 = 3.33.

t-statistic = (mean1 - mean2)/SE = (23.7 - 24.9)/3.33 = (-1.2)/3.33 = -0.360. So t ≈ -0.36. Degrees of freedom = n1+n2-2 = 18.

Two-tailed p-value: For t=0.36, df=18, p ~ 0.72? Let's approximate: t=0.36 is small. Using t distribution, p ~ 0.72. So not significant at 0.05 or 0.01.

If using Welch's t-test: SE_welch = sqrt(s1^2/n1 + s2^2/n2) = sqrt(57.57/10 + 53.21/10) = sqrt(5.757 + 5.321) = sqrt(11.078) = 3.33 (same). df_welch = (s1^2/n1 + s2^2/n2)^2 / [ (s1^2/n1)^2/(n1-1) + (s2^2/n2)^2/(n2-1) ] = (11.078)^2 / [ (5.757^2)/9 + (5.321^2)/9 ] = 122.8 / [ (33.15)/9 + (28.30)/9 ] = 122.8 / [ 3.683 + 3.144 ] = 122.8 / 6.827 = 18.0. So df ~18. So same.

Thus p-value ~0.72. So fail to reject null at both levels.
